raw_response:
I have farmed here a long time, so I would keep the wheat-maize rotation as the backbone of my land use and leave only a smaller area for cotton. With 15 mu total, I would put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 10 mu, and keep 5 mu for cotton. I would do this because wheat and maize are steadier for my conditions in Quzhou County, I have well irrigation, and with some family labor working off-farm I would not push too much land into cotton since cotton needs more careful field work and picking. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability, keep fertilizer at a moderate but reliable level, irrigate enough to avoid drought stress, and use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and saves time. I would not chase the highest possible input level; I would aim for a stable harvest, manageable labor, and lower risk across the whole year.
